Seminar Title:

Design and Development of Efficient Control Methods for Hybrid Active Power Filters to Improve Power Quality

Seminar Type:

Synopsis Seminar

Department:

Electrical Engineering

Speaker Name:

Pavankumar Daramukkala ( Rollno : 519ee1001)

Speaker Type:

Student

Venue:

EE401 (Electrical Engg. Department)

Date and Time:

04 Nov 2026 3:30 pm

Contact:

Kanungo Barada Mohanty

Abstract:

The increasing use of nonlinear loads, power-electronic converters, and renewable-energy systems has made power-quality improvement essential in modern electrical distribution networks. Conventional passive filters are economical but sensitive to parameter variations and resonance, while shunt active power filters offer dynamic compensation at higher converter ratings and operating costs. A shunt hybrid active power filter (SHAPF) combines passive and active filtering to achieve effective harmonic mitigation with reduced active-converter burden. This thesis aims to develop an effective multi-layer control framework for SHAPF-based power-quality improvement, with an ultimate application to a grid-connected solar photovoltaic (PV)-fed system. First, an adaptive estimation-based harmonic identification method is investigated to identify dominant load-current harmonics under varying operating conditions. The estimated harmonic information is utilized to optimize passive-filter design, considering filter tuning, reactive-power compensation, component constraints, resonance, and active-converter rating. Second, a robust nonlinear adaptive filtering method is developed for accurate fundamental-component separation and harmonic extraction under load variations, measurement noise, and nonideal supply conditions. Its effectiveness is evaluated against conventional and adaptive methods using estimation accuracy, convergence, transient response, and compensation-reference quality. Third, advanced nonlinear, adaptive, sliding-mode, and predictive controllers are investigated for SHAPF DC-link voltage regulation to ensure stable energy balance and effective filtering operation. These controllers are compared in terms of settling time, overshoot, steady-state error, voltage ripple, disturbance rejection, parameter sensitivity, and implementation complexity. Fourth, an advanced nonlinear model predictive current-control strategy is developed using a discrete-time converter model and cost-function-based switching-state selection. Improved dead-time compensation is incorporated to enhance current tracking and mitigate inverter nonidealities, with performance assessed through tracking error, harmonic distortion, dynamic response, and computational requirements. Finally, the most suitable methods are integrated into a hybrid multi-layer control architecture for a grid-connected PV-fed SHAPF, coordinating PV power variation, harmonic compensation, DC-link regulation, and predictive converter control. The integrated framework is evaluated under steady-state and dynamic conditions, including nonlinear-load changes and PV operating variations, using verified simulation and, where available, real-time or experimental results. The intended contribution is a systematic design-and-control methodology targeting reduced source-current distortion, improved power factor, effective reactive-power compensation, stable DC-link voltage, fast dynamic response, and reduced active-converter burden through coordinated multi-layer control.
